name: Node.js
summary: A JavaScript host runtime that combines V8 execution with a phase-oriented event loop, microtask and nextTick queues, and cached CommonJS module loading.

features.name: Phase-oriented asynchronous I/O loop
features.description: Node.js organizes asynchronous work around libuv event-loop phases including timers, pending callbacks, poll, check, and close callbacks. The poll phase retrieves I/O events and executes their callbacks, while setImmediate callbacks run in the check phase.
benefits: Provides a deterministic scheduling vocabulary for non-blocking I/O callbacks
Allows kernel or libuv work to progress without blocking the JavaScript thread
costs: Long-running callbacks delay later phases and timers
Phase ordering and platform differences complicate latency reasoning

features.name: Priority nextTick and microtask queues
features.description: Node.js drains the nextTick queue and V8 microtasks between event-loop operations. Its fixed queue is processed before the next loop phase, and recursive nextTick scheduling can starve I/O progress.
benefits: Supports callbacks after the current stack unwinds while preserving ordering guarantees
Integrates promise microtasks with Node-specific asynchronous APIs
costs: Unbounded nextTick work can prevent the poll phase from running
Multiple scheduling queues require explicit reasoning about priority

features.name: Cached CommonJS module loader
features.description: The CommonJS loader resolves a request, returns exports from Module._cache when available, inserts a newly created module into the cache before evaluation, and removes it if evaluation throws. An unfinished cached module can be returned for circular dependencies.
benefits: Avoids re-evaluating the same resolved module
Provides a concrete partial-state mechanism for cyclic dependencies
costs: Module identity depends on resolution and filename details
Consumers of a cycle can observe partially initialized exports

mathematical_views.question: How do phase queues, nextTick callbacks, and microtasks transition toward the next asynchronous I/O opportunity?
assumptions: The documented phases are modeled as ordered states with callback queues
Callbacks execute synchronously within a phase until that phase's queue or callback limit permits transition
The model abstracts libuv internals and platform-specific phase details

mathematical_views.question: How do resolution, cache insertion, evaluation, and failure transitions determine CommonJS module identity and cyclic loading behavior?
assumptions: Resolved filenames are graph node identities
The module cache is a mutable map from resolved identity to module state
The view covers the CommonJS loader path and not every ESM loader hook

benefits: Non-blocking I/O organized into explicit phases
costs: Callback duration and phase ordering affect latency

benefits: Stable reuse of loaded module instances
